system.name: AWMSystem (TP-MDDN benchmark)
system.one_liner: Autonomous decision-making navigation system with LLM-based subtask decomposition, goal selection and completion monitoring for multi-demand navigation with task preferences.

content.variant_note: three question-titled panels, each a user and robot exchange on a real example, beside a performance panel with a scatter plot and a bar chart
content.argues: Three LLM-driven decisions (choose a subtask, generate dual-tempo actions, check completion) yield a 16% higher success rate than DDN and InstructNav under the TP-MDDN benchmark, with better efficiency than InstructNav.
content.subject: Three tinted dialogue panels (choose subtask, dual-tempo actions, completion check) beside a scatter plot and a bar chart.

lessons.what_to_learn: Title each overview panel with the question it answers and fill it with a short exchange between a fixed pair of avatars on a real example, so every module reads as one capability; put a results panel with a trade-off scatter plot (gain arrow, Desirable arrow) and a bar chart in the same figure.
lessons.suits: Agent or embodied-AI papers whose system is a few LLM decisions that can each be shown with a real prompt and answer, plus a headline efficiency and accuracy result.

evidence: The pink area shows subtask selection using landmark semantic memory
the green area details dynamic subtask completion checks.
Our method achieves a 16% higher success rate than DDN [1] and InstructNav [2] under the TP-MDDN benchmark

summary: TP-MDDN is a benchmark for long-horizon navigation with several demands and explicit task preferences, and AWMSystem is the paper's autonomous decision-making system built from LLM modules, a semantic memory map and a dual-tempo action generator. Figure 1 has two lettered sections. In (a) Overview, three tinted panels titled by questions (choose a subtask, generate dual-tempo actions, check completion) each stage a user and robot dialogue with real prompts and answers: landmark semantic memory built from observations and a point cloud, generalist and specialist policy boxes, a status prompt and answer. In (b) Performance, a scatter plot of success against time with a +16% arrow and a bar chart compare Ours with DDN, MO-DDN and InstructNav.
summary_zh: TP-MDDN 是多需求导航基准，AWMSystem 是其决策系统。图 1 的 (a) 用三块以问题命名的彩色面板，以用户与机器人对话展示选子任务、双节奏动作和完成检查；(b) 用散点图和柱状图对比 DDN 等基线。
notes: The pre-screen order (contribution-mosaic, actor-interaction, worked-walkthrough) is kept; the three question panels are counted as panels together with the blue results panel, and the letters (a) and (b) head sections that group them. The meaning of the headset-person icon (user or navigating agent) is not stated. Generalist as zero-shot planning and specialist as fine control follow the abstract, not the figure.
